terms.definition: A single model call enhanced with retrieval, tools or memory. It does one bounded job, and control flow doesn't branch on what the model decides.
terms.architect_significance: The simplest pattern; the starting point before workflows or agents.
terms.exam_relevance: Pick it for well-defined, verifiable single-step tasks.
terms.common_confusion: Calling any tool-using call an "agent". If your code controls the flow, it isn't one.
terms.source: M1 Pattern Selection; Official – Building effective agents

terms.definition: A system where the model decides its own sequence of tool calls toward a goal. The control flow lives inside the model.
terms.architect_significance: Unlocks open-ended work, but its autonomy is your liability surface. It needs budgets, permission limits and stopping criteria.
terms.exam_relevance: Use only when the path can't be listed in advance and errors can be recovered.
terms.common_confusion: "Open-ended feeling" isn't the same as "unenumerable steps".

terms.definition: Steps orchestrated in your own code along predefined paths; each step may or may not call Claude.
terms.architect_significance: Testable, loggable, auditable; the default when the steps are knowable.
terms.exam_relevance: "Auditor asks which step approved it" → workflow.
terms.common_confusion: Rebuilding a workflow inside an agent loop with guardrail tools.

terms.definition: A structured test set that pairs inputs with expected outputs or criteria and produces a score you can compare across changes.
terms.architect_significance: The acceptance criteria and the gate for every model, prompt or retrieval change.
terms.exam_relevance: Write evals before production code, and keep them current.
terms.common_confusion: Manual spot checks aren't an eval.

terms.definition: Give each agent, subagent or user only the capabilities its task requires.
terms.architect_significance: Removing a capability eliminates its risk; monitoring only compensates for it.
terms.exam_relevance: Remove unneeded tools rather than logging or confirming their use.
terms.common_confusion: Treating confirmation prompts as least privilege.

terms.definition: The model's active attention space, measured in tokens. Content outside it doesn't exist for the model, and it resets between calls.
terms.architect_significance: A hard edge for both capability and billing.
terms.exam_relevance: Budget below the ceiling; measure tokens rather than estimating them.
terms.common_confusion: Thinking the window is a memory, or a data-governance boundary.

terms.definition: Next-token prediction, knowledge, working memory and steerability. Each is a capability paired with a limitation and a mitigation.
terms.architect_significance: The lens for decomposition, feasibility and risk.
terms.exam_relevance: Map the symptom to the property, then to the compensating control.
terms.common_confusion: Treating the properties as flaws to fix rather than forces to design around.
terms.source: M1 How Claude Behaves; M2 Feasibility

terms.definition: A deliberate point where a person reviews or approves model output, placed by risk and reversibility.
terms.architect_significance: Focuses limited reviewer attention on high-stakes decisions.
terms.exam_relevance: Pre-action approval for irreversible actions; sampling for low-stakes ones.
terms.common_confusion: Routing everything to review causes consent fatigue.

terms.definition: The ability to see what the system is doing, reconstruct why, and detect when it goes wrong.
terms.architect_significance: A precondition for letting agents act; LLMs fail quietly.
terms.exam_relevance: Log request, response, context and outcome; use a shared trace ID across agents.
terms.common_confusion: Error-rate dashboards alone don't count as observability.

terms.definition: Reusing a processed, stable prompt prefix across requests to cut cost and latency. The response is identical either way.
terms.architect_significance: The biggest lever when a long, stable prefix is reused often.
terms.exam_relevance: Static content first, then the breakpoint, then dynamic content; check TTL and write cost.
terms.common_confusion: Caching answers rather than prefixes; caching rarely called prompts.

terms.definition: Data that changes during a conversation or process (order status, balances, inventory), owned by a system of record.
terms.architect_significance: Must be fetched by a tool call, not retrieved from an index.
terms.exam_relevance: "Answer contradicts the database" → you need a tool call.
terms.common_confusion: Shortening the index refresh to "fix" stale live state.

terms.definition: Claude calls external functions or APIs during a response and uses the results.
terms.architect_significance: Turns text generation into action, which is why side-effecting tools need authorization.
terms.exam_relevance: The mechanism for live state and deterministic computation.
terms.common_confusion: MCP vs. tool use. MCP shares tools across clients, and those tools are invoked through tool use.

terms.definition: The AI Fluency competency of deciding which work Claude should own, which humans keep, and which is collaborative.
terms.architect_significance: Produces the delegation map.
terms.exam_relevance: Justify by reversibility, stakes and accountability.
terms.common_confusion: Can Claude do it vs. should Claude own it.

terms.definition: The AI Fluency competency of stating precisely what you want: scope, format, constraints. It applies both to prompts and to stakeholders.
terms.architect_significance: Separates prompts that hold in production from demo prompts, and it's how decisions land with stakeholders.
terms.exam_relevance: Underspecification is the failure it prevents.
terms.common_confusion: More words isn't more description.

terms.definition: Judging output quality (acceptable, needs revision, needs override) rather than accepting it at face value.
terms.architect_significance: Feeds evals and monitoring; also spots unequal treatment.
terms.exam_relevance: Teams without it watch metrics move without checking the outputs.
terms.common_confusion: Confirming a value was produced isn't judging whether it's right.

terms.definition: Taking responsibility for verifying and vouching for AI outputs, and keeping human accountability checkpoints in place.
terms.architect_significance: Becomes a verification checklist and review gates.
terms.exam_relevance: Watch for automation pressure eroding oversight.
terms.common_confusion: Faster shipping isn't the same as trustworthy shipping.

terms.definition: Splitting a request into what Claude does, what existing systems do and what humans do, then breaking Claude's share into steps or units.
terms.architect_significance: Over-assigning to Claude is the most common and most expensive early mistake.
terms.exam_relevance: Assign each part to an owner before picking a pattern.
terms.common_confusion: Task decomposition vs. ownership decomposition. Both matter.

terms.definition: One of three outcomes: feasible as scoped, feasible with constraints, or not feasible. Each comes with its load-bearing constraints.
terms.architect_significance: A verdict without constraints doesn't survive production.
terms.exam_relevance: Gather volume, input size and latency before issuing one.
terms.common_confusion: Capability isn't feasibility.

terms.definition: The stated conditions under which an architecture works or doesn't (e.g. documents up to N pages).
terms.architect_significance: Written into the SOW so both sides know what's in scope.
terms.exam_relevance: An undocumented constraint becomes a production failure.
terms.common_confusion: Treating boundaries as risks to mention verbally.

terms.definition: A proven wiring for a recurring problem class: agent, RAG, document pipeline (evaluator-optimizer), routing/triage, coding agent.
terms.architect_significance: Teams have already learned what breaks in each.
terms.exam_relevance: Most common misuse: retrieval applied to live state.
terms.common_confusion: Reference ≠ blueprint; adapt it to the workload.

terms.definition: A workflow where each call processes the previous output, with programmatic gates between steps.
terms.architect_significance: Predictable sequences with checkpoints.
terms.exam_relevance: Fixed sequence plus checks → chain.
terms.common_confusion: Chaining independent steps that could run in parallel.

terms.definition: Classify the input, then dispatch it to a specialised downstream path, model or handler.
terms.architect_significance: Separation of concerns; lets cheaper tiers handle easy cases.
terms.exam_relevance: Distinct categories and accurate classification.
terms.common_confusion: Building an agent for what is really four routes.

terms.definition: Running independent subtasks at once (sectioning) or the same task several times for confidence (voting).
terms.architect_significance: Speed and confidence.
terms.exam_relevance: Only for independent units.
terms.common_confusion: Parallelization (subtasks fixed in advance) vs. orchestrator-workers (subtasks decided at runtime).

terms.definition: A central model decomposes work at runtime, delegates to workers or subagents, and synthesises their results.
terms.architect_significance: Handles work that's too large or too varied for one context.
terms.exam_relevance: Subtasks not known in advance.
terms.common_confusion: Assuming coverage instead of reconciling it.

terms.definition: One step generates, another evaluates against criteria, and the loop refines.
terms.architect_significance: Common in document pipelines where a first pass isn't reliable.
terms.exam_relevance: Clear criteria plus measurable gains from refinement.
terms.common_confusion: Using it without reliable evaluation criteria.

terms.definition: Split a large work item into independent units, dispatch one subagent per unit, then synthesise.
terms.architect_significance: Clean per-unit contexts plus concurrency.
terms.exam_relevance: Reconcile results returned against units dispatched.
terms.common_confusion: "48 reviewed" when 50 were dispatched.

terms.definition: A synthesis rule requiring results returned to equal units dispatched, and flagging any gap.
terms.architect_significance: Prevents a confident summary over incomplete work.
terms.exam_relevance: The fix for silently dropped subagent units.
terms.common_confusion: Assuming every subagent returns something.

terms.definition: The agent that owns the goal; it decomposes, delegates and synthesises, but doesn't do sub-task work itself.
terms.architect_significance: Its failure is often unrecoverable, so protect and checkpoint its state.
terms.exam_relevance: Recoverable subagent failure vs. unrecoverable orchestrator failure.
terms.common_confusion: Letting the orchestrator do the sub-task work.

terms.definition: An agent with its own context that owns one scoped sub-task and returns a structured result.
terms.architect_significance: Failures are usually recoverable; tools should be scoped to the task.
terms.exam_relevance: Make subagent work idempotent and give it least-privilege tools.
terms.common_confusion: Putting compliance-critical checks in subagents instead of deterministic code.

terms.definition: Efficiency, transformation, productivity, cost (the run cost of the solution) and performance SLAs.
terms.architect_significance: Keeps ROI claims in the sponsor's language.
terms.exam_relevance: Tag each value claim with its pillar.
terms.common_confusion: Efficiency (same work, cheaper) vs. transformation (work that wasn't possible before).

terms.definition: Measured baseline → projected state in the same unit (including review effort) → minus run cost from sizing → payback with sensitivity.
terms.architect_significance: Turns "can we build it?" into "is it worth building?".
terms.exam_relevance: Common traps are an estimated baseline, assuming full automation, and average-based cost.
terms.common_confusion: Build cost (counted in payback) vs. run cost.

terms.definition: Training a model variant on task data. Access is limited, and it locks you to a fixed model version.
terms.architect_significance: The last step after prompting, tools and stronger patterns.
terms.exam_relevance: Justified only for very high volume, critical latency, or format consistency that prompting couldn't achieve.
terms.common_confusion: Reaching for it first when prompting "isn't reliable".

terms.definition: The Claude model family, trading capability against cost and latency.
terms.architect_significance: Not choosing a tier means defaulting to the most expensive one.
terms.exam_relevance: Start from a baseline tier (Sonnet per M1; Opus 5.5 per current docs) and move only on eval evidence, per step and per category.
terms.common_confusion: Judging a downgrade on its average score.

terms.definition: The pass/fail line for a change, set before the eval runs.
terms.architect_significance: Stops teams negotiating with themselves after seeing the data.
terms.exam_relevance: A partial migration can follow from per-category failures.
terms.common_confusion: Setting the threshold after the results are in.

terms.definition: A separate reasoning pass in thinking tokens (billed as output) before the answer. On current models, adaptive thinking with output_config.effort replaces budget_tokens; Claude 4.7 and later reject manual budget_tokens with a 400.
terms.architect_significance: A cost and latency trade-off.
terms.exam_relevance: Enable it only for a measured accuracy gap, after prompt work.
terms.common_confusion: "It can't hurt"; enabling it on classifiers.

terms.definition: Fixing the model version in configuration, monitoring deprecations, and keeping an update runbook.
terms.architect_significance: Makes changes attributable and governed.
terms.exam_relevance: An unpinned version that rolled forward is a governance gap.
terms.common_confusion: Thinking pinning is a pattern choice. It's an operational discipline.

terms.definition: A designed, reusable asset stating role and scope, constraints and an output contract.
terms.architect_significance: Ambiguity is a defect multiplied across every request.
terms.exam_relevance: Underspecification produces inconsistent outputs.
terms.common_confusion: A system prompt isn't an enforcement layer.

terms.definition: A prompt with parameterised slots inside fixed scaffolding that carries the safety and consistency guarantees.
terms.architect_significance: Makes the safe path the default path.
terms.exam_relevance: Filling a slot must not remove a constraint.
terms.common_confusion: Free-form slots placed above the guardrails.

terms.definition: The required shape of a response (fields, format, citations), stated in the prompt and validated afterwards.
terms.architect_significance: Lets guardrails be structural rather than just prose.
terms.exam_relevance: Enforce "never promise X" through the format, plus screening.
terms.common_confusion: Stating rules only in the role text.

terms.definition: A gap in a prompt that the model fills with its own assumption, differently each time.
terms.architect_significance: The main source of variation in reused prompts.
terms.exam_relevance: Diagnose by asking, for each requirement, "stated or only hoped for?".
terms.common_confusion: Blaming the model tier for it.

terms.definition: Instruction only; a handful of examples; step-by-step reasoning before the answer.
terms.architect_significance: Each step up adds tokens and latency.
terms.exam_relevance: Start zero-shot, add examples for format, add CoT for multi-step reasoning.
terms.common_confusion: CoT everywhere; using few-shot for arithmetic precision.

terms.definition: The property describing the context window's hard edge. Things work until they abruptly don't.
terms.architect_significance: Over-limit requests fail in specific, recognisable ways.
terms.exam_relevance: 400 means too many tokens; 413 means too many bytes; model_context_window_exceeded means generation hit the ceiling.
terms.common_confusion: Mixing up a rejected request with a mid-generation stop.

terms.definition: Ways to measure actual tokens before sending a request and on every response.
terms.architect_significance: Limits and billing apply to measured counts.
terms.exam_relevance: Measure, don't estimate by characters.
terms.common_confusion: Fixed characters-per-token ratios.

terms.definition: The boundary between the cacheable prefix and dynamic content, and how long the cache entry lives: 5-minute default (write 1.25×), or 1-hour (write 2×); reads 0.1× of base input.
terms.architect_significance: Prefix order and call frequency decide whether caching pays off.
terms.exam_relevance: "A cache that never hits" means dynamic content came first.
terms.common_confusion: Assuming a longer TTL fixes a changing prefix (the 1-hour TTL doubles the write cost and still misses a changing prefix).

terms.definition: A versioned, self-contained unit (SKILL.md plus optional scripts) that packages a repeatable procedure. On the API it's attached via container.skills and needs the Code Execution Tool.
terms.architect_significance: Governed reuse across teams; loads progressively.
terms.exam_relevance: Repeatable, distributed and governed → Skill; flexible and local → prompt library.
terms.common_confusion: Assuming the platform screens Skills for you.

terms.definition: A shared collection of prompt fragments that engineers assemble in their own code.
terms.architect_significance: Lightweight reuse within one team.
terms.exam_relevance: Lean toward it for flexible, frequently tweaked prompts.
terms.common_confusion: Using it where versioned rollback is needed.

terms.definition: Periodically summarising accumulated context so long sessions keep going.
terms.architect_significance: Controls growth, but it's lossy and mostly one-way.
terms.exam_relevance: Preserve identifiers, numbers and decisions verbatim.
terms.common_confusion: Treating summaries as faithful by default.

terms.definition: An agent configured with more tools or permissions than its task requires (exam term; the modules describe it as least-privilege tool configuration).
terms.architect_significance: Larger attack surface, higher cost, worse tool selection.
terms.exam_relevance: Remove out-of-scope tools and record why.
terms.common_confusion: Deferring tool loading doesn't reduce permissions.

terms.definition: Scoping each subagent's tools to its task so it can't reach tools the orchestrator or other roles hold.
terms.architect_significance: Contains compromised or erring subagents.
terms.exam_relevance: Subagents that inherit every tool are a red flag.
terms.common_confusion: Shared toolsets "for simplicity".

terms.definition: The server injects verified user identity and role, from SSO or auth, into the system prompt. It never comes from the user's message.
terms.architect_significance: Prevents spoofed roles.
terms.exam_relevance: "As a manager, show me…" in user text is a red flag.
terms.common_confusion: Authentication (who you are) vs. authorization (what you may do).

terms.definition: A deterministic check (allowlist plus identity and scope) before any side-effecting action.
terms.architect_significance: Provable, replayable, auditable.
terms.exam_relevance: Output screening can't stop an action that has already run.
terms.common_confusion: Letting the model judge whether the caller is authorised.

terms.definition: A protected HTTP MCP server's role: it accepts access tokens, publishes Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), and clients send tokens on every request.
terms.architect_significance: Standard per-user authorization for remote tools.
terms.exam_relevance: Replaces static shared secrets for non-public data.
terms.common_confusion: MCP authorization is optional in the spec; that's not the same as unnecessary.

terms.definition: A separate API key per tenant in a multi-tenant deployment.
terms.architect_significance: Attribution and isolation for rate limits and cost.
terms.exam_relevance: A shared key means one tenant's spike hits everyone, invisibly.
terms.common_confusion: Logging a tenant_id field doesn't give you isolation.

terms.definition: The latency 95% of requests complete within.
terms.architect_significance: SLA breaches come from the slow tail.
terms.exam_relevance: Design against p95, not the median.
terms.common_confusion: p50 and the median are the same thing.

terms.definition: Telling apart model drift, data drift and model-update effects when a metric moves.
terms.architect_significance: Each has a different fix.
terms.exam_relevance: Needs version and prompt IDs plus distribution comparison.
terms.common_confusion: Fixing before attributing.

terms.definition: Model drift: the model's outputs on stable inputs change over time. Data drift: the input distribution changes.
terms.architect_significance: Gradual, so threshold alerts often miss them.
terms.exam_relevance: Use periodic distribution comparison.
terms.common_confusion: Both differ from a model version update.

terms.definition: A per-request record (model, version, tokens, latency, stop reason, tool calls), with one ID propagated across all agents in a run.
terms.architect_significance: Makes a multi-agent run reconstructable.
terms.exam_relevance: The fix for fragmented logs.
terms.common_confusion: Separate per-agent dashboards don't replace it.

terms.definition: Chunk and index a corpus ahead of time, retrieve relevant chunks at query time, and pass them into context.
terms.architect_significance: For stable knowledge, large corpora, and citations.
terms.exam_relevance: Not for live state. Measure retrieval separately from generation.
terms.common_confusion: Similarity isn't truth.

terms.definition: Splitting the corpus into retrievable units: uniform spans, meaning-based breaks, or structure-preserving sections.
terms.architect_significance: Choose by the structure of the source.
terms.exam_relevance: Hierarchical for contracts, manuals and policies.
terms.common_confusion: One default chunk size for everything.

terms.definition: Dense (embeddings) matches meaning; sparse (e.g. BM25) matches exact tokens; hybrid combines both.
terms.architect_significance: Choose by query pattern.
terms.exam_relevance: Identifiers being missed → add sparse.
terms.common_confusion: Dense-only for part numbers.

terms.definition: A low-tuning way to merge ranked lists by scoring each item on its rank in each list.
terms.architect_significance: The defensible default for hybrid retrieval.
terms.exam_relevance: Hybrid → fuse with RRF.
terms.common_confusion: Averaging raw similarity scores across different indexes.

terms.definition: An open protocol for exposing tools, prompts and resources from a server so any MCP-aware client can use them.
terms.architect_significance: Build once, connect from many clients.
terms.exam_relevance: Use when two or more clients need the same tools.
terms.common_confusion: MCP as the default integration; MCP as an agent loop.

terms.definition: A managed agent loop (iteration, tool execution, termination), the same one behind Claude Code, embedded in your own application. Available for TypeScript and Python.
terms.architect_significance: Multi-turn agents inside your product without building the loop yourself.
terms.exam_relevance: Agent SDK vs. Anthropic SDK (a wrapper with no loop).
terms.common_confusion: You give up fine-grained control between turns.

terms.term: Entry point / build-time interface / delivery route
terms.definition: Three layers. The entry point is how users reach Claude; the build-time interface is what engineers code against; the delivery route is where API traffic terminates (first-party, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry).
terms.architect_significance: Three decisions, made for three different stakeholders.
terms.exam_relevance: Compliance eliminates routes and entry points first.
terms.common_confusion: "It's all Claude."

terms.definition: Protocols for delegating tasks between independently owned agents (e.g. the A2A protocol announced by Google, positioned as complementary to MCP).
terms.architect_significance: Cross-organisation or cross-framework delegation.
terms.exam_relevance: Source gap: no official Anthropic documentation; the decision principle is inferred.
terms.common_confusion: In-process subagents (agents you own) vs. external agents.

terms.definition: Monolithic loads everything up front; progressive stages context, carrying forward only what the next step needs.
terms.architect_significance: Monolithic is the silent budget killer in long sessions.
terms.exam_relevance: Production usually combines a monolithic prefix, progressive state, retrieval and compaction.
terms.common_confusion: Strategy and sizing are separate decisions.

terms.definition: Lets Claude search a large tool catalogue and load only the tools it needs. Tools marked defer_loading: true load only when discovered.
terms.architect_significance: Progressive discovery for tools; cuts definition overhead.
terms.exam_relevance: Keep 3–5 hot tools loaded; never defer the search tool; still send full definitions.
terms.common_confusion: Deferring a tool doesn't remove its permissions.

terms.definition: Skills show only metadata up front; SKILL.md and referenced files load when needed.
terms.architect_significance: Hundreds of Skills without filling the context.
terms.exam_relevance: An example of progressive discovery.
terms.common_confusion: Loading every Skill's full content up front.

terms.definition: A labelled, representative set of inputs (including edge cases and adversarial items) that evals run against.
terms.architect_significance: An unrepresentative set makes scores meaningless.
terms.exam_relevance: Keep it current with every prompt or model change.
terms.common_confusion: Building it from a few convenient inputs.

terms.definition: A model that scores outputs against a rubric, for interpretive qualities.
terms.architect_significance: Scales interpretive grading.
terms.exam_relevance: Needs a rubric, constrained verdicts, reasoning, human calibration and a different grader model.
terms.common_confusion: Trusting an uncalibrated judge.

terms.definition: Code-based grading first, an LLM judge when interpretation is needed, humans as the last resort.
terms.architect_significance: The cheapest reliable method for each behaviour.
terms.exam_relevance: Favour volume over perfection.
terms.common_confusion: Judging schema validity with a model.

terms.definition: Checking a judge's verdicts against human-labelled outputs before relying on it.
terms.architect_significance: An uncalibrated judge is worse than none because it looks trustworthy.
terms.exam_relevance: "Judge says great, experts disagree" → calibrate.
terms.common_confusion: Averaging repeated judge runs doesn't calibrate anything.

terms.definition: Scoring whole conversations for context retention, invented details, and quality as length grows.
terms.architect_significance: Single-turn sets miss conversation failures.
terms.exam_relevance: Needs its own transcript dataset.
terms.common_confusion: Adding more single prompts instead.

terms.definition: The share of responses containing information unsupported by the input, the source data or allowed logic.
terms.architect_significance: A key accuracy metric with a threshold.
terms.exam_relevance: Fix through grounding, not instructions.
terms.common_confusion: Hallucination (ungrounded content) vs. prompt failure (an ambiguous instruction).

terms.definition: Prompt failure, hallucination, model mismatch, orchestrator-workers failure.
terms.architect_significance: Each class has its own fix.
terms.exam_relevance: Classify before you fix.
terms.common_confusion: Rewording a prompt to cure a grounding problem.

terms.definition: The wrong tier for the task, or a tier swapped without re-evaluation.
terms.architect_significance: Category-specific regressions after a cost-driven swap.
terms.exam_relevance: Remedy with eval-gated selection and per-category routing.
terms.common_confusion: Mistaking it for data drift.

terms.definition: A hypothesis, random sticky assignment, a pre-specified primary metric, and a sample size calculated for higher LLM variance.
terms.architect_significance: Separates improvements from noise.
terms.exam_relevance: Watch for underpowered tests and outcome-shopping.
terms.common_confusion: Statistical significance vs. practical worth.

terms.definition: Run the new version on copied live traffic while users get the current version, and score the shadow outputs offline.
terms.architect_significance: Validates without exposing users.
terms.exam_relevance: Regulated settings, low traffic, or high per-output risk.
terms.common_confusion: A canary still exposes real users.

terms.definition: Asynchronous bulk processing at a discount (50% of standard prices; up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch; results within 24 hours).
terms.architect_significance: Cuts cost when the SLA allows waiting.
terms.exam_relevance: Confirm compliance coverage before routing regulated data through it.
terms.common_confusion: Using it for interactive paths.

terms.definition: A cost model from call volume, the token distribution, model tier and sensitivity analysis, built before any code.
terms.architect_significance: The average token count understates heavy tails by two to three times.
terms.exam_relevance: Model the distribution, not the average.
terms.common_confusion: Treating POC bills as a forecast.

terms.definition: A mapping from technical metrics (task success, latency) to business KPIs (first-contact resolution, handle time).
terms.architect_significance: Lets sponsors see value with a live query.
terms.exam_relevance: Build it at design time.
terms.common_confusion: Giving sponsors raw technical dashboards.

terms.definition: Training-time alignment is the constitution-shaped safety behaviour that applies to every request. Inference-time control is the deployment-specific screening, authorization and review you build.
terms.architect_significance: Claude can't enforce a rule it was never given.
terms.exam_relevance: A domain policy must live in a layer you build.
terms.common_confusion: "It refuses harmful prompts, so our policy is covered."

terms.definition: The written document Anthropic trains Claude against: broadly safe, ethical, guideline-compliant and helpful, weighed holistically.
terms.architect_significance: Reduces broad harm; doesn't encode your policy.
terms.exam_relevance: Training-time, not deployment-time.
terms.common_confusion: Treating it as a runtime control.

terms.definition: Checks before the model call (should this reach the model?) and before the response returns (is this safe to return?).
terms.architect_significance: Two of the three control points.
terms.exam_relevance: Chain model-based and deterministic checks.
terms.common_confusion: One output filter isn't a guarded path.

terms.definition: When an operator-built guardrail errors, traffic either passes unscreened (open) or is blocked (closed).
terms.architect_significance: Failing open looks protected but does nothing.
terms.exam_relevance: Fail closed where a wrong pass causes harm.
terms.common_confusion: Applies to your components, not Anthropic's API-level controls.

terms.definition: Malicious instructions arriving through retrieved documents or tool outputs rather than from the user.
terms.architect_significance: The dominant injection vector in RAG and agent deployments.
terms.exam_relevance: Screen retrieved and tool content before adding it to context.
terms.common_confusion: Screening only user input.

terms.definition: Oversized or padded inputs that consume context or output budget, truncating work or inflating cost.
terms.architect_significance: A cost and availability risk.
terms.exam_relevance: Input limits, max_tokens, per-turn budgets.
terms.common_confusion: Mistaking it for hallucination.

terms.definition: The API's stop_reason "refusal" when streaming classifiers intervene, with stop_details always present on a refusal; category and explanation can be null.
terms.architect_significance: Lets the app route refusals by class.
terms.exam_relevance: Branch on stop_reason, not on a populated category; reset the refused turn before continuing.
terms.common_confusion: Hard-coding category lists (verify current docs).

terms.definition: Auditing Skill bundles for anomalous or out-of-scope behaviour, running them with least privilege in a sandbox, and sourcing them from trusted registries.
terms.architect_significance: Skills are distributable code with hidden behaviour.
terms.exam_relevance: Record a verdict: approve, reject or remediate.
terms.common_confusion: Assuming the platform screens Skills.

terms.definition: A written record of each risk's category, component, likelihood and impact, control, owner and evidence.
terms.architect_significance: What the security reviewer signs.
terms.exam_relevance: Verbal discussion doesn't count.
terms.common_confusion: A diagram isn't a risk assessment.

terms.definition: Sending decisions to people by stakes (reversibility and cost) and calibrated confidence.
terms.architect_significance: Spends limited reviewer attention well.
terms.exam_relevance: Low confidence plus irreversible or high-cost → human first.
terms.common_confusion: Routing by volume.

terms.definition: Oversight breaking down when reviewers approve so many items that they stop reading.
terms.architect_significance: Turns review into rubber-stamping.
terms.exam_relevance: Move review to plan or exception checkpoints.
terms.common_confusion: Adding more approvers to fix it.

terms.definition: A HIPAA contract that lets a vendor process PHI. Coverage is specific to the configuration and feature.
terms.architect_significance: Without it, the route is non-compliant.
terms.exam_relevance: Beta features are generally excluded unless explicitly listed.
terms.common_confusion: One BAA assumed to cover every configuration.

terms.definition: Processing and storing data, including logs and caches, within an approved region, configured at the integration layer.
terms.architect_significance: Rules out routes that can't pin the region.
terms.exam_relevance: An EU pin needs a region-pinned CSP route; direct-API inference_geo offers only "us" or "global" (verified 2026-11-19).
terms.common_confusion: Forgetting log and cache copies.

terms.definition: A table mapping each obligation to a technical control, an owner and an evidence artifact.
terms.architect_significance: The auditable form of compliance.
terms.exam_relevance: Revalidate on a schedule; configurations drift.
terms.common_confusion: A compliant route isn't proof.

terms.definition: Proof that a control is live: a signed agreement, a configuration screen, an authorization record, a log query.
terms.architect_significance: What reviewers accept.
terms.exam_relevance: A design document is a claim, not proof.
terms.common_confusion: Vendor certifications on their own.

terms.definition: Passing only the fields the language task needs, using reference IDs where possible, and redacting PII before the call.
terms.architect_significance: Prevents PII from reaching request logs.
terms.exam_relevance: "If the task doesn't need it, it isn't in the context."
terms.common_confusion: Encrypting logs instead of not logging the data.

terms.definition: Where unequal outcomes enter: the retrieval corpus, prompt framing, few-shot examples, downstream routing.
terms.architect_significance: Makes fairness something an architect can instrument.
terms.exam_relevance: Look here when the model passed the vendor's bias evals.
terms.common_confusion: Assuming fairness is the vendor's job.

terms.definition: Capturing inputs, retrieved context, output and routing per decision so it can be replayed and explained.
terms.architect_significance: Serves users, regulators and the build team.
terms.exam_relevance: The log is itself governed sensitive data.
terms.common_confusion: Aggregate metrics can't reconstruct a single decision.

terms.definition: Listen, translate, write down, across four buckets: must do, must not do, must cost, must prove.
terms.architect_significance: Sets the constraints the design follows.
terms.exam_relevance: Finish all four buckets before sketching anything.
terms.common_confusion: A discovery call that turns into a design session.

terms.definition: One row per item: the statement as said, the implied constraint, the architectural decision, and the assumption to confirm.
terms.architect_significance: Keeps the reasoning traceable into design.
terms.exam_relevance: Label assumptions as assumptions.
terms.common_confusion: Writing preferences down as requirements.

terms.definition: A requirement traces to something the stakeholder said; an assumption is something the design takes for granted.
terms.architect_significance: Unsourced assumptions are the most dangerous kind.
terms.exam_relevance: Assumptions need an owner and confirmation.
terms.common_confusion: Burying assumptions as facts.

terms.definition: What it costs to undo a decision after the system has been built around it.
terms.architect_significance: The trade-off element that changes the meeting.
terms.exam_relevance: Gain, give-up, reversal cost (plus compliance effect in regulated settings).
terms.common_confusion: Per-call cost vs. the business total at volume.

terms.definition: Signals → Triage → Decide → Act → Review; a table mapping each signal to a trigger, an owner, an action and any scheduled checkpoint.
terms.architect_significance: Monitoring isn't a feedback loop.
terms.exam_relevance: Include slow-drift triggers and scheduled regulated checkpoints.
terms.common_confusion: Dashboards with no owners.

terms.definition: Names what is measured, what counts as a breach, and what happens on a breach. Thresholds trace to UX expectations, business criticality or eval acceptance criteria.
terms.architect_significance: Makes expectations enforceable and defensible.
terms.exam_relevance: Arbitrary thresholds are a red flag.
terms.common_confusion: An SLA with no stated consequence.

terms.definition: Each decision recorded with its date, the rejected alternatives and the trade-off it resolved.
terms.architect_significance: Stops successors reversing decisions that matter.
terms.exam_relevance: Diagram-only handoffs fail the safe-change test.
terms.common_confusion: A "what" without a "why".

terms.definition: Can a competent architect who wasn't in the room make a safe change after reading the document?
terms.architect_significance: The definition of done for handoff.
terms.exam_relevance: Serve three readers: handoff recipient, compliance reviewer, returning architect.
terms.common_confusion: Measuring completeness by page count.

terms.definition: Use case and scope, the metric before, the metric after, an auditable control, a measurement owner (plus optional, Partner-Track reuse potential).
terms.architect_significance: Makes value legible to a CFO.
terms.exam_relevance: Technical metrics alone fail.
terms.common_confusion: Volume and latency aren't business outcomes.

terms.definition: A written record of which entry point or route owns which task, and why, made before integration.
terms.architect_significance: Prevents scope drift between routes.
terms.exam_relevance: Multi-platform deployments need one.
terms.common_confusion: Leaving routing logic undocumented.

terms.definition: Discovery → design → handoff → monitoring → iteration.
terms.architect_significance: Knowing the phase tells you when to move on, or go back.
terms.exam_relevance: Changed constraints → re-architect, not iterate.
terms.common_confusion: Skipping the handoff phase.

terms.definition: Cost, latency (p95), reliability and failure modes are all invisible in a demo.
terms.architect_significance: A POC proves capability only.
terms.exam_relevance: Add a cost model, reliability controls, pinning, evals and observability.
terms.common_confusion: Treating a demo bill as a forecast.

terms.definition: Retries with exponential backoff near the API call; a circuit breaker at the service boundary; fallback chains in orchestration.
terms.architect_significance: Graceful degradation instead of total failure.
terms.exam_relevance: Each control works only at the right layer.
terms.common_confusion: Retrying non-transient 4xx errors.

terms.definition: Trips when a dependency's error rate passes a threshold, so requests fail fast for a cooldown period.
terms.architect_significance: Stops one degraded dependency taking down the system.
terms.exam_relevance: Sits at the service boundary.
terms.common_confusion: Circuit breakers vs. retries.

terms.definition: A team baseline (project CLAUDE.md, agreed tools and MCP servers, permission posture) that everyone starts from.
terms.architect_significance: Prevents drifted personal setups.
terms.exam_relevance: Review and version it once for everyone.
terms.common_confusion: Each engineer configuring their own.

terms.definition: Enable one champion per team first to prove a workflow, then seed adoption batch by batch.
terms.architect_significance: Local experts and examples; avoids lumpy adoption.
terms.exam_relevance: Better than a mass switch-on.
terms.common_confusion: Equating access with adoption.

terms.definition: A bundle of Skills assigned to a group or org, with install preferences and version-controlled updates from a repository.
terms.architect_significance: The strongest governance for group-scoped distribution.
terms.exam_relevance: The fix for a "shipped with no way back" Skill.
terms.common_confusion: Org-provisioned Skills have no native rollback.

terms.definition: Model defaults, model allowlists, effort guidance, and spend, rate and per-user caps, set during team setup.
terms.architect_significance: Unmanaged model choice multiplies cost at team scale.
terms.exam_relevance: Set it before the first bill.
terms.common_confusion: Reviewing quarterly instead.

terms.definition: A markdown file loaded at session start with standing instructions and project conventions.
terms.architect_significance: A shaping layer.
terms.exam_relevance: Not a guarantee; use hooks for things that must always happen.
terms.common_confusion: Shaping vs. governing layers.

terms.definition: A script that fires on Claude Code lifecycle events as a deterministic gate the agent can't skip.
terms.architect_significance: The guarantee comes from code rather than the prompt.
terms.exam_relevance: "Must always run X before Y" → hook.
terms.common_confusion: Relying on CLAUDE.md instructions instead.

terms.definition: default, acceptEdits, plan, auto (a classifier reviews each action), dontAsk (locked-down CI), bypassPermissions (containers or CI only).
terms.architect_significance: Governs what the agent may do without prompting.
terms.exam_relevance: Use bypassPermissions only in isolated environments.
terms.common_confusion: Behaviour changes over time; verify current docs.

terms.definition: The correctness, security, maintainability and human-understanding checks AI-generated output must pass before production.
terms.architect_significance: Turns diligence into a repeatable gate.
terms.exam_relevance: The merger must be able to explain the code.
terms.common_confusion: Passing tests ≠ understood.

terms.definition: Lumpy adoption: a few heavy users, the rest barely engaged. Stalling at chat: never moving beyond Q&A to tools, repository context or Skills.
terms.architect_significance: The two common adoption failures.
terms.exam_relevance: Fix with champions and workflow integration.
terms.common_confusion: Restricting access as a response.

terms.definition: A runbook captures known symptom → cause → action paths; an escalation path says who handles what, and when.
terms.architect_significance: Builds team self-sufficiency.
terms.exam_relevance: Teach the path rather than firefighting.
terms.common_confusion: The architect fixing every incident personally.

terms.definition: A temporary failure (429 rate limit, timeout, 5xx including 529 overloaded) that's likely to succeed on retry.
terms.architect_significance: Retry with exponential backoff.
terms.exam_relevance: Don't retry 4xx validation errors such as a 400 for a prompt that's too long.
terms.common_confusion: 429 (throttled) vs. 400 (invalid request).
